grh_41e936beb32b5db79642.title: Mercury Theater 1938-08-08 (5) I'm a Fool, My Little Boy, Open Window
paragraphs: A Mercury Theatre anthology presenting three separate short stories. Sherwood Anderson's I'm a Fool follows a young racetrack worker who invents a false identity to impress a girl and later regrets that the lie ruined his chance to know her honestly. Saki's The Open Window centers on a nervous visitor whom young Vera convinces that men returning toward an open window are ghosts, sending him fleeing when the very-much-alive men appear. Carl Ewald's My Little Boy is an affectionate and comic meditation by a father observing his independent, mischievous son and resolving to help him discover moral truths for himself rather than simply accept what adults teach him.

This [[show|the-mercury-theatre-on-the-air|The Mercury Theatre on the Air]] broadcast aired on August 8, 1938. It is listed as episode 5 in the archive. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes [[person|orson-welles|Orson Welles]], Edgar Barrier, Ray Collins, William Allen, and Brenda Forbes. Other credited names include Dan Seymour as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 59 minutes.

This version is based on [[work|work.mercury.03efc19eaa6976ff|Mercury Theater 1938-08-08 (5) I'm a Fool, My Little Boy, Open Window]]. Saki is credited as author and Sherwood Anderson is credited as author.

grh_417db55a2482ccc61f05.title: The Value of a Hunch
paragraphs: A sheriff becomes suspicious of Sutherland's supposedly therapeutic drug-rehabilitation ranch after strange nighttime activity and a group of men who remind him of a violent California cult. Weeks of surveillance reveal odd tire tracks, military-style trucks and an offshore ship, convincing him that something large is being smuggled ashore. When an amphibious craft finally lands, the sheriff expects weapons but discovers crates packed with high-grade marijuana instead. A raid arrests twelve men and seizes more than thirteen million dollars worth of drugs, though Sutherland escapes in the confusion. Hours later the fugitive unknowingly hitches a ride with the sheriff, pulls a gun, and surrenders only after the lawman bluffs that a hidden weapon in the car is aimed at him.

grh_4188f44d2ddbc7cccc10.title: Should Old Acquaintance Be Forgot
paragraphs: Middle-aged newlyweds Fred and Margaret discover after their impulsive marriage that each has left behind a long-standing almost-fiancé: Jane in Fred's case and Tom in Margaret's. Jealousy and old habits complicate the honeymoon as the former partners remain very much in their lives, but the awkward foursome gradually rearranges itself. Jane and Tom become attracted to one another and leave together on a South Seas cruise, while Fred and Margaret accept that their wounded egos are part of the adjustment and settle into the comic work of learning how to live together.

grh_417d606f926b27f6e869.title: Wanda
paragraphs: A teenage patient named Jane insists that she has a sister named Wanda, even though her family and medical records say no such sister exists. Psychiatrist Crane Shaker follows Jane's memories instead of treating them only as a delusion, tracing them to two sisters named Jane and Wanda Webber who died in an automobile accident eighteen years earlier. Jane recognizes their graves, former home and details she should not know, and confronting that earlier tragedy finally ends her obsession with finding Wanda.
